entries.answer: Procrastination is delaying a task you intend to do, and it is not primarily a time-management failure. The common cause is that the task gives immediate discomfort and no immediate reward, while avoidance gives immediate relief. That is why the hardest tasks get done last and the whole evening disappears. The workable counter is to lower the entry cost rather than to fight the feeling, so a two-minute start counts as having done it.

patterns: how to revise for an exam
entries.answer: Spaced repetition reviews material at increasing intervals, timed so that each review happens just as you are about to forget it. It works because recall strengthens memory more than re-reading, and because the spacing is what forces the strengthening. Practically it means scheduling review for the next day, then three days, then a week, rather than reading everything the night before an exam.

patterns: how do i focus while studying
entries.answer: The Pomodoro technique is a simple timer: work on one task for twenty-five minutes, take five minutes off, and after four cycles take a longer break. The value is not the numbers but the fact that a large task becomes small enough to start, which is the step most people cannot take. It also produces a record of how long things actually take, which is usually more accurate than someone's guess.

entries.answer: Active recall means testing yourself rather than rereading, and it is consistently the highest-return study method. Rereading produces a feeling of familiarity that is easy to mistake for knowledge, and familiarity is not recall. Closing the notes and writing what you remember finds the gaps immediately, which is uncomfortable and is the point, because a gap found while studying is a gap found before the exam.

patterns: how should i take notes while studying
entries.answer: Note taking fails when it becomes transcription, because copying a paragraph feels productive and produces nothing retrievable later. The alternative is to write notes in your own words and in a form you can test from, so that a page of notes becomes a set of questions rather than a set of facts. Cornell-style splitting - cues on one side, notes on the other - exists for exactly this reason.

patterns: how do i stop getting distracted
entries.answer: Deep work is sustained concentration on a cognitively demanding task while unproductive activity is out of reach. The reason it is rare is not laziness but that switching cost is low and every interruption has to be paid for twice, once to stop and again to restart. Batching communication rather than answering it continuously, and leaving a phone in another room, both work because they remove the choice rather than relying on willpower.
